newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Gas oil stocks still hold centre stage in Europe.
newsitem.headline: Gas oil stocks still hold centre stage in Europe.

text.p: Gas oil will remain centre stage among European Union November stocks data released on Tuesday, but analysts also say they are more interested than normal for the season in crude and gasoline inventories.
Analysts also cautioned against an immediate reaction to the Europe-wide figures. The effects of the French lorry drivers strike on French stocks may distort the overall picture, they said.
The main question was whether the middle distillate stock build seen in October continued through November.
"Gas oil is still the one to watch," said Geoff Pyne, energy analyst at UBS.
"(The figures) should provide us with the first real sign of the extent to which they (distillate stocks) are tight at the start of winter," said Keith Hamm of oil consultants, Petroleum Economics.

Distillate stocks in the 14 countries of the European Union, excluding Sweden, rose by 6.60 million barrels in October to 291.45 million barrels, according to Stitchting Euroilstock's last stocks report. However, despite the build, the stock level was still 21.65 million barrels down year-on-year.

Analysts, cautious of any firm forecasts, tentatively predict that distillate stocks will be flat to slightly up. They reason that temperatures throughout western Europe were relatively mild and prices were sufficiently high to have discouraged most buying.
"French and German consumers also stocked up quite considerably in September and October," said Peter Bogin of Cambridge Energy Research Associates.
German end-user stocks were at around 65 percent of capacity at the end of October, almost unchanged from the end-September figure.
Meanwhile, EU gasoline stocks may well have fallen in November as arbitrage to the United States was viable for much of the month, analysts reason.

However, the same analysts say they expect some regional variation. In the United Kingdom, majors and refiners built stocks ahead of the end-of-month budget. In France, the lorry drivers strike may also have caused product to build at refineries.
"All of those (factors) will have created some interest in gasoline,... not least because it has been the co-pilot of gas oil in the last month," said Bogin.
At the end of October, EU gasoline inventories fell by 3.74 million barrels to 153.00 million barrels, leaving them 2.97 million barrels higher than in October 1995.

The French lorry drivers strike could muddy the picture both for gasoline stocks and for diesel, and thus distillate stocks. The drivers caused 12 days of road blockages in the second half of November.
"We might have to be careful... (the figures) could be so distorted by the French strike," said Hamm.
November crude stock figures will also hold some interest. In the past few months, stocks have been sharply down year-on-year, but production is believed to be up in the last quarter of the year.
At the end of October, crude stocks were a mere 80,000 barrels down at 401.06 million barrels, but were 15.35 million barrels lower than at the end of October 1995.
